purpose: Separate supplied vague-metric data and proved consequences from existence of that data, so theorem/kernel status does not conflate them.

nodes.title: Countable-test vague metric specification
nodes.statement_tex: A regular Euclidean measure is a positive Borel measure equipped with regularity. A vague metrization consists of compactly supported continuous tests $f_j$, a metric on these measures whose distance is $\sum_{j\geq0}2^{-(j+1)}\min(1,|\int f_j\,d\mu-\int f_j\,d\nu|)$, cutoff tests majorizing $1$ on each positive-radius closed ball and nonnegative everywhere, and equivalence between metric sequential convergence and vague convergence for every sequence of regular measures.
hypotheses: The metric and all of its specifications are explicit fields; the definition chooses no data from an existence theorem.
nodes.status_note: Definitions contain no placeholders. This is data/specification, not a claim that such data exist.

nodes.title: Existence of a countable-test vague metric
nodes.status_note: Canonical proof now complete and exact-source kernel checked with only standard axioms. Separate-module integration pending CI. Keeping existence separate remains useful for reusable conditional results.

nodes.title: Consequences of a supplied vague metric
nodes.statement_tex: For supplied $M:\mathrm{VagueMetrization}(n)$, metric convergence is equivalent to vague convergence; its countable-test distance separates measures; and every compact family has a finite cover by metric balls of every positive radius, with centers in that family.
hypotheses: M : VagueMetrization n is supplied explicitly.
The finite-cover conclusion assumes the family is compact in M.metric.
nodes.status_note: Canonical proofs already kernel-checked; no dependence on exists_vagueMetrization.
